citations.citation: For the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, in which Katori's concept of trapping many neutral atoms free of Doppler, recoil and light-shift errors was developed by Ye and collaborators into clocks with 10^-18 accuracy and stability, enabling millimetre-scale tests of gravitational redshift and searches for variation of constants.

for the invention of the optical lattice clock, trapping many neutral atoms at a magic wavelength where the lattice does not shift the clock transition, and for realizing it at a fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, enabling millimetre-scale tests of gravitational redshift and sensitive searches for variation of constants

for the invention and realisation of the optical lattice clock, in which neutral atoms trapped at the magic wavelength reach a fractional uncertainty near 10^-18 and open millimetre-scale tests of gravitational redshift and of the constancy of fundamental constants
for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, bringing the measurement of time and frequency to the 10^-18 level
